audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is called a line you dodge — 'blink to dodge his E line' in mid, 'dodge his charged E' in whys[4], spikes[1] and wants.you[1].
audit.why: It is not a line and there is nothing to sidestep. Riot's text: 'Vladimir pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood which, when released, deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units.' It detonates around HIM, and enemy units block it. That last clause is the whole counterplay to his laning phase and it is not written anywhere on the page: keeping a minion between you and Vladimir blanks the poke outright, which is a completely different early game to the one the page teaches (walk sideways and hope). It also costs him health to charge, which is why he is willing to spam it into a passive lane and why he needs Transfusion up.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood bursts in an area around Vladimir and enemy units block it — stand behind a minion and the poke never reaches you. It costs him health to charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool is described five times as being on 'its long cooldown' and the number is never given, and the untargetable window is never timed either.
audit.why: It is 28/25/22/19/16 seconds and the untargetability lasts 2 seconds, at 350 range. Both halves are actionable and both are missing. Twenty-eight seconds at rank 1 is the largest exploitable gap in the lane for a champion who needs one clean commit; and 2 seconds is short enough that a stacked Riftwalk chain does not have to abort — you wait it out standing on him rather than backing off, which is the opposite of what 'untargetable dodge, every commit is a coin flip' implies.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 350 range, and only 2 seconds of untargetability. Bait it, count 28, and commit — or simply outlast the 2 seconds standing on top of him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hemoplague does not appear anywhere on the page. Vladimir's level 6 is absent from a matchup whose entire thesis is that level 6 is your flip.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Vladimir infects an area with a virulent plague. Affected enemies take increased damage for the duration. After a few seconds, Hemoplague deals magic damage to infected enemies and heals Vladimir for each enemy Champion hit', 120s flat, 625 range. The damage amplification is the part that matters to a Kassadin: inside Hemoplague every point of his poke and every point of his jungler's gank hits harder, so the level 6 window the page tells you to take is exactly the window in which he gains a damage multiplier. A flat 120s cooldown is also the longest number in the matchup and therefore the cleanest green light.
audit.corrected: Hemoplague is 120s flat and amplifies all damage you take inside it before detonating and healing him. His 6 answers your 6 — never take the flip while it is up.

audit.why: Sides left untouched and they hold up: Vladimir owns 1-5 on free-to-cast poke against a mana champion, level 6 is Skill because both ultimates arrive together (which is more true than the page knew, since it had not noticed Hemoplague), and he reclaims the item stages as an AP hard-scaler. 55.26% over 38 games is a real sample but it is a whole-game number, not a lane-stage one.

The Void Stone framing is right for once and I kept it: every point of Vladimir's damage is magic, so the passive reduction and the Null Sphere shield both apply in full. This is the matchup where that line earns its place, which is why I left the 15% figure alone rather than stripping it.

Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield. It has never silenced in this kit version, and silence is a flag the kit builder tracks, so its absence is meaningful rather than unknown.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.whatIsWrong: The flagged needs-antiheal interaction (Transfusion, Hemoplague) has no home on this page.
audit.why: Transfusion is a 4.6-second heal at rank 5 that costs him nothing, and Hemoplague heals him per champion hit. Against a champion whose entire lane is drain-sustain, Grievous Wounds timing genuinely decides extended trades. I did not force it into a string I was already rewriting for other reasons — the Itemization row is where it belongs and that row is not otherwise wrong, so flagging it here is more honest than padding an unrelated edit.
audit.corrected: Itemization should name anti-heal against Transfusion and Hemoplague.

audit.why: 55.26% over 38 games; the page quotes no figure. No change.

edits.before: Both of us are weak at level 1, but Vlad edges the next two levels — his charged E (Tides of Blood) and Q (Transfusion) drain out-trade my single mana-hungry Null Sphere, and I have no W (Nether Blade) yet to refund the mana I spend. Do not throw Q to trade; you will go OOM and he heals it off with his Q on minions. Farm passively, eat the poke, and remember my Void Stone passive cuts his magic damage by 15% (he has no such reduction against me) — so this is a patience phase, not a fight phase. Bank XP and wait for your spikes.
edits.after: Both of you are weak at level 1, but Vlad edges the next two levels — Tides of Blood (E) and the Transfusion (Q) drain out-trade your single mana-hungry Null Sphere, and you have no Nether Blade yet to refund what you spend. Tides of Blood bursts in an area around HIM and enemy units block it, so keep a minion between you and the poke never lands. Void Stone cuts his damage by 15% because all of it is magic, and his casts cost him no mana — this is a patience phase. Bank XP and wait for your spikes.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — Q maxed plus Nether Blade let me farm under tower, but I'm not all-inning a Vlad who can charge-poke with E and Q-sustain through it. The lane flips at 6: Riftwalk is mobility, not just burst — blink to dodge his E line, or jump him when his W Sanguine Pool is on its long cooldown. Bait the pool first, because once it's down he's immobile and can't escape. By my first stall item (Rod of Ages) the 15% magic reduction plus Null Sphere's shield blank most of his poke and I reach even.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — a maxed Q plus Nether Blade let you farm under tower, but you are not all-inning a Vlad who charge-pokes with E and sustains on a 4.6-second Transfusion. The lane flips at 6: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and buys only 2 untargetable seconds, so bait it, count it, then blink in while he is immobile. Hemoplague lands at 6 too, on a flat 120s, and it amplifies every point of damage you take inside it — never take the flip while it is up.

edits.before: Riftwalk finally gives you a blink to dodge his charged E and jump him when Sanguine Pool is on its long cooldown — your first window to flip from prey to threat.
edits.after: Riftwalk lets you jump him the moment Sanguine Pool is spent — 28s at rank 1, and only 2 untargetable seconds, so count it out and go. Your first flip from prey to threat.

edits.before: Riftwalk gives you the mobility to dodge his charged E and dive him when Sanguine Pool's long cooldown is down — your first real flip.
edits.after: Riftwalk lets you dive the second Sanguine Pool is spent — 28s at rank 1, 2 untargetable seconds — but Hemoplague answers at 6.

edits.before: Full-build Vlad pools (untargetable) under your Riftwalk dive and kites your blinks with Rylai's slow — he is the rare scaler who out-lives your assassin burst window.
edits.after: Full-build Vlad pools for 2 untargetable seconds under your Riftwalk dive and kites your blinks with Rylai's — the rare scaler who out-lives your whole burst window.

edits.before: Hold W Sanguine Pool to go untargetable under your Riftwalk dive and dodge your burst
edits.after: Hold Sanguine Pool for its 2 untargetable seconds under your Riftwalk dive and eat the burst

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. It governs your forward steps. - Q shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 2 untargetable seconds — bait it before you spend your kill window. Hemoplague is a flat 120s and amplifies damage. - Q shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for real fights.

edits.before: Track Vladimir’s Sanguine Pool: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 2s untargetable. Tides of Blood bursts around him and enemy units block it — hold a minion between you.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Two untargetable seconds on a 28s cooldown at rank 1 — bait it before you spend your kill window, then commit.

edits.before: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Q-silence the counterplay, and leave before the fight even registers you.
edits.after: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Null Sphere to interrupt a channel, and leave before the fight registers you.

notes: Hemoplague was completely absent from this matchup before this pass — no spike, no cooldown row, no mention in any of the seven why-rows — which is a strange gap on a page that names level 6 as the flip. Worth checking whether other Kassadin matchups are missing the enemy ultimate entirely; a cheap script over the packet's enemyAbilities R-slot against each page's text would find them. The other thing a human should decide: Itemization for this matchup does not mention anti-heal even though Transfusion (free, 4.6s at rank 5) and Hemoplague both heal him — I left that row alone rather than rewrite an otherwise-correct string just to fit the point in.
